State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Bajaj Allianz Genearal Insurance ... vs Dipak Manikrao Lodage, on 16 February, 2021
1 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

 Date of filing :05.02.2019
 Date of order :16.02.2021

 MAHARASHTRA STATE CONSUMER DISPUTE
 REDRESSAL COMMISSION,MUMBAI, BENCH AT
 AURANGABAD.

FIRST APPEAL NO. : 206 & 290 OF 2019
IN COMPLAINT CASE NO.: 72 OF 2018
DISTRICT CONSUMER FORUM : AURANGABAD.

1) FIRST APPEAL No.206/2019
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company,
Through its Divisional Manager,
Plot No.D-5/1, ABC EAST, 3rd floor,
Chikalthana, Aurangabad. 431210 APPELLANT
 VERSUS
Deepak Manikrao Lolge,
R/o Flat No.B-601, Marvel Azure,
Sade Satara Nali, Hadapsar, Pune-411028. RESPONDENT

 Present : Adv.S.G.Chapalgaonkar for appellant.
 Adv.S.D.Gaikwad for respondent.

2) FIRST APPEAL No.290/2019
Deepak Manikrao Lolge,
R/o Flat No.B-601, Marvel Azure,
Sade Satara Nali, Hadapsar, Pune-411028. APPELLANT
 VERSUS
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company,
Through its Divisional Manager,
Plot No.D-5/1, ABC EAST, 3rd floor,
Chikalthana, Aurangabad. 431210 RESPONDENT

 Present : Adv.S.D.Gaikwad for appellant
 Adv.S.G.Chapalgaonkar for respondent.
 2 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

CORAM : Smt.S.T.Barne, Hon`ble Presiding Judicial Member.
 Mr.K.M.Lawande, Hon'ble Member.

 JUDGMENT
(Delivered on 16/02/2021)

Per Smt.S.T.Barne, Hon'ble Presiding Judicial Member.
1. The appellant Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd,. in
appeal No. 206/2019 and appellant Deepak Manikrao Lolge in appeal
No. 290/2019, have preferred their respective appeals against
judgment and order in consumer complaint No. 72/2018 decided by
District Consumer Forum, Aurangabad on 2.11.2018.
2. Shri. Deepak Manikrao Lolge is the complainant and Bajaj
Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd,. is the opponent in original
complaint No.72/2018 before District Consumer Forum, hence, they
are hereinafter referred as complainant and opponent as per their
status in the complaint.
3. It is the case of complainant Deepak Manikrao Lolage that he is
the owner of Maruti Ritz car MH-12-LD-5647. Said car was insured
with opponent Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company for the
period of 26.8.2015 to 25.08.2016. Said car met with an accident on
15.5.2015 at Isarwadi Fata, Tq. Gangapur, Dist.Aurangabad on
Ahmadnagar-Aurangabad high way. The intimation of accident was
given by complainant to insurance Company. On completing
formalities said car was taken to Diwekar Auto Motor Pvt. Ltd,.
Aurangabad for repairing. The opponent has also appointed
surveyor, who carried preliminary survey. Said car is still lying with
the said service station and repairing work is pending. It is the
 3 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

contention of the complainant that the accident took place on
15.11.2015. However, the opponent Insurance Company wrote
closure letter to complainant on 29.5.2017, and repudiated the claim
on the ground that, "the accident took place on 15.11.2015 and
intimation given to Insurance Company on 2.1.2016, that is after
lapse of 48 days, which deprived them an opportunity to inspect the
car on the spot and to ascertain the facts including but not limited to
the cause, nature and quantum of loss, which is required to decide
admissibility of the claim leading to the violation of policy condition
No.1, which requires in writing to the company immediately upon the
occurrence of accident or loss or damage in the event of any claim
and thereafter the insured shall give all such information and
assistance as company shall require. Further the insured at material
time of accident used the insured vehicle for hire and reward, which
is in violation of condition as to limitation as to use of vehicle. The
company shall not be liable to pay compensation, in violation of
aforesaid conditions as per the provisions of policy. The opponent
Insurance Company further mentioned in the said letter that in view
of observation, which is not received any clarification the claim is
repudiated and closed without payment."
4. It is further contention of complainant that he is doing private
job and remains busy. He has paid premium of Rs. 12,633/- of
insurance through agent of opponent company. The friends of the
complainant were occupying the vehicle. They were coming from
Pune to Aurangabad, driver was having valid license. The motor cycle
rider of Honda motorcycle bearing registration No. MH-20-DU-8446,
was proceeding towards Ahmadnagar from Aurangabad with high
 4 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

speed, and the vehicle met with an accident due to the rash driving
of both the drivers. In the said accident vinod Ashok Pardeshi the
friend of complainant died on the spot, and the wife of other friend
namely Sow.Maya Bhalerao and his son got injured. There was no
breach of policy condition. The claim is repudiated by opponent
Insurance Company on the technical ground, and there is deficiency
in service on the part of opponent. Hence, he has filed consumer
complaint before District Consumer Forum, claiming Rs. 5,50,000/-
towards damages and mental, physical agony.
5. The opponent Insurance company gave appearance before
District Consumer Forum and filed it's written statement. The copy
of said written statement is at page No.47 of appeal compilation. It is
the contention of the opponent company that the vehicle MH-12-LD-
5647 was duly insured with Insurance Company under private car
package policy, as per terms and conditions specifically mentioned in
the policy. The insurance policy specifically speaks about limitation
as to use of the vehicle only for social domestic and pleasure purpose
for insured business. The insured has used the vehicle during policy
period, for carrying passengers on hire and reward basis. On
15.11.2015 the vehicle was travelling on Pune to Aurangabad road,
and near Issarwadi fata, the insured vehicle met with an accident in
which passenger Vinod Ashok Pardeshi died and other passengers
namely Maya Yogesh Bhalerao and her son Sanvidhan Yogesh
Bhalerao were injured. The aforesaid accident took place on
15.11.2015. The FIR is registered on 16.11.2015. However, no
intimation was given to opponent Insurance Company till 2.1.20216.
There was delay of 48 days in intimating to the company.
5 FA/206 & 290 of 2019
6. It is the contention of the opponent that it was obligatory on
the part of insured to give immediate intimation to Insurance
Company. The very object behind it is that the insurer shall get the
opportunity to examine damage caused to the vehicle, immediately
after the incident. The insurer should get opportunity to find
whether vehicle used as per terms and condition of the policy. The
opponent on receiving intimation, has issued communication dated
19.4.2017 and 15.5.2017 thereby calling explanation from
insured/complainant regarding aforesaid facts. However, insured
failed to give explanation. Hence, on 29.5.2017 opponent Insurance
Company repudiated the claim.
7. It is the contention of opponent Insurance Company that they
have appointed the IRDA approved surveyor after receipt of
intimation. He found that vehicle was removed from the spot long
back and it was not possible to find actual loss suffered in the
accident or otherwise. It is further contention of the opponent that
in pursuance of the registration of FIR in crime No.242/15 at police
station, Waluj, the statement of occupant were recorded. In the said
statement Sow.Maya Yogesh Bhalekar admitted that she was
travelling as fair paying passenger. The opponent Insurance
Company has rightly repudiated the claim. There is no deficiency in
service on the part of opponent Insurance Company. Hence, the
opponent Insurance Company has prayed for dismissal of consumer
complaint.
6 FA/206 & 290 of 2019
8. The District Consumer Forum after giving opportunity to the
parties of hearing, pleased to allow the claim partly on non standard
basis, and pleased to allow 75 % of the amount of Rs. 1,61,398/- from
the date of repudiation of claim with 6% interest p.a. and Rs.5,000/-
towards the mental agony.
9. Being aggrieved by the said order, the original opponent Bajaj
Allianz Insurance Company has preferred appeal No.206/2019 on the
following grounds.
That, the opponent Insurance Company has come with two
fold defence that firstly the complainant has used private car for
carrying passengers for hire and reward, and as such is guilty of
breach of policy condition. The second contention is regarding delay
in giving intimation to opponent Insurance Company about the
incident which is condition No.1 in general condition of policy. The
complainant gave intimation to opponent Insurance company after
48 days on 2.1.2016 of accident which took place on 15.1.2015. The
District Consumer Forum should have been appreciated that the
insurance company shall have opportunity to take survey of vehicle
immediately after the incident. In this case the opponent Insurance
Company has lost this opportunity as intimation is given after 48
days.
10. The District Consumer Forum ought to have appreciated that
the opponent Insurance Company has given two communications
and offered opportunity to complainant to give explanation if any for
causing delay in giving intimation as to loss. But complainant failed
 7 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

to give explanation, which itself vitiates the claim of complainant.
The District Consumer Forum has ignored the said defences.
11. The District Consumer Forum exceeded its jurisdiction in
directing the insurer to settle the claim on non standard basis. When
the facts of this case were not fit in the guidelines laid down in the
case of
Amalendu Sahu Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd
,. by
Hon'ble National Commission. The order of District Consumer
Forum is liable to be set aside in view of the judgments of Hon'ble
National Commission, in 1) Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd,.
Vs. Gurshinder Singh reported in 1215(2) CPR 149, 2) Jaspal Kaur
Vs. New India Assurance Company reported in 2015(2) CPR 140,
which are not even referred by the District Consumer Forum in its
order. Hence, the opponent Insurance Company has prayed for
quashing of judgment and order of the District Consumer Forum.
12. The complainant has come with appeal No.A/290/2019 on the
following grounds.
That, the Insurance Company though alleged that there is
breach of policy condition, and repudiated the claim by letter dated
29.5.2017, it is false and baseless. The opponent Insurance Company
has repudiated the claim on technical ground, which amounts to
deficiency in service on the part of opponent. There is no wilful
breach of policy condition on the part of insured. The claim cannot
be repudiated on the technical reasons, as per the guidelines of IRDA.
13. It is also contention of complainant that the District Consumer
Forum, Aurangabad has not considered the evidence in proper
 8 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

perspective. Hence, the appellant/original complainant has prayed
for setting aside the order and to allow the complaint as prayed.
14. On the aforesaid respective submissions of the parties,
following points arise for our determination. We have noted them
along with our findings against those accordingly for the reasons to
follow.
Sr.No. Points. Findings.
 1. Whether, there is deficiency in service No.
 on the part of opponent?

 2. Whether, there requires interference Yes.
 in the judgment and order of District
 Consumer Fourm?

 3. What relief and order? As per final order.

 REASONS
15. Points No.1to3 :- Heard learned Adv.Shri.Gaikwad and Adv.
Shri.Chapalgaonkar on their respective submissions on behalf of
complainant and opponent in respective appeal. They both argued
the matter in the line of respective pleadings and respective grounds
of appeals.
16. To avoid the repetition of discussion we would like to mention
the undisputed fact that, it is not disputed that the complainant is
the owner of the Maruti Ritz vehile bearing registration No. MH-12-
LD-5647. Said car was insured with opponent Insurance Company for
the period of 26.8.2015 to 25.8.2016 and during existence of policy
 9 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

said vehicle met with an accident, on 15.5.2015 at Isarwadi fata
Tq.Gangapue, Dist.Aurangabad on Aurangabad-Ahmadnagar road.
The FIR came to be registered with police station on 16.5.2015 by ASI
on behalf of State. In the said accident one of the passenger Vinod
Pardeshi died on the spot and one Maya Bhalerao and her son were
injured.
17. It is submitted on behalf of complainant that, the incident of
accident is genuine. There is immediate FIR to police. The
complainant submitted claim to opponent with all required
documents. However, the opponent repudiated the claim on
technical ground, said repudiation letter which at page No. 35 of
appeal compilation in appeal No. 206/2019 stating that, i) the
intimation is given on 2.1.2016, i.e. after 48 days of the incident. ii)
that, the vehicle run for hire and reward. The opponent Insurance
Company cannot deny the claim on technical ground. Thus, on
repudiating the claim the complainant has claimed deficiency in
service. Hence, reliance is placed on following reported cases.
1) Omprakash Vs. Reliance General Insurance Company
in (A.No.
 15611/2017 out of SLP (C) No. 742 of 2015 ) decided by
 Hon'ble Supreme Court on 4.10.2017, wherein delay of 8 days
 was in giving intimation to police and the Insurance Company ,
 the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed in para 11 as follows-
11. it is Common knowledge that a person who lost his vehicle
 may not straightway go to the Insurance Company to claim
 compensation. At first, he will make efforts to trace the
 vehicle. It is true that the owner has to intimate the insurer
 immediately after the theft of the vehicle. However, this
 10 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

 condition should not bar settlement of genuine claims
 particularly when the delay in intimation or submission of
 documents is due to unavoidable circumstances. The decision
 of the insurer to reject the claim has to be based on valid
 grounds. Rejection of the claims on purely technical grounds in
 a mechanical manner will result in loss of confidence of policy-
 holders in the insurance industry. If the reason for delay in
 making a claim is satisfactorily explained, such a claim cannot
 be rejected on the ground of delay. It is also necessary to state
 here that it would not be fair and reasonable to reject genuine
 claims which had already been verified and found to be correct
 by the Investigator. The condition regarding the delay shall not
 be a shelter to repudiate the Insurance claims which have been
 otherwise proved to be genuine. It needs not emphasis that
 the
Consumer Protection Act
aims at providing better
 protection of the interest of consumers. It is a beneficial
 legislation that deserves liberal construction. This laudable
 object should not be forgotten while considering the claims
 made under the Act.
18. Reliance is also placed on
Amalendu Sahoo Vs. Oriental
Insurance Company
ltd,. (A.No.2703/2010 decided on 25.3.2010,
wherein the Hon'ble N.C. relied upon the judgment of S.C. & gave
guideline about setting of claim on non standard basis in following
cases.
Sr.No. Description. Percentage
 settlement.
 (i) Under declaration of licensed carrying Deduct 3 years'
 capacity. difference in premium
 11 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

 from the amount of
 claim or deduct 25 %
 of claim amount,
 whichever is higher.
 (ii) Overloading of vehicles beyond licensed Pay claims not
 carrying capacity. exceeding 75 % of
 admissible claim.
(iii) Any other breach of warranty/condition Pay upto 75% of
 of policy including limitation as to used. admissible claim.
19. With aforesaid submissions the complainant supported the
judgment of District Consumer Forum to the extent of deficiency in
service on the part of opponent in allowing the claim. But he has
come with appeal challenging the quantum awarded which is not in
accordance with estimation and compensation is not in the
proportionate with loss and mental agony.
20. On the other hand, the learned Adv. for appellant
Shri.Chapalgaonkar has submitted that, accident took place on
15.11.2015. The intimation is given on 2.1.2016 after 48 days of the
incident, with which there is breach of general condition No.1
mentioned in the policy which at page No. 67 of compilation in
appeal No. 206/2019. The policy is produced at page No. 62 to 69
along with terms and condition. Secondly, it is Private Car Package
Policy, the complainant has used the vehicle for hire and reward, in
violation of the terms and condition pertaining to limitation to use
the vehicle. Therefore, the opponent gave letter to the complainant
dated. 14.4.2017 by giving opportunity to complainant to explain on
aforesaid counts. And the complainant failed to give any explanation
to the letter dated 14.4.2017. Therefore, the opponent Insurance
Company has issued another letter on 15.5.2017 and gave another
 12 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

opportunity to the complainant. Then the opponent Insurance
Company for breach of policy conditions and for non explanation to
the letters above issued by opponent to complainant, the opponent
Insurance Company rightly repudiated the claim.
21. The learned Adv. for opponent Insurance Company
placed
reliance upon
the judgment of State Consumer Dispute Redressal
Commission, Maharashtra State, in New India Assurance Company
Vs. Raghunath Dnyanu Khambe reported in 2019 STPL 3592MH (I
(2019) CPJ 139) wherein the Hon'ble State Commission relied upon
the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance
Company Ltd,. Vs. Mena Agrawal reported in III (2009) SLT 158/2009
(2) SCC 523) and held that, when the vehicle insured was used on hire
basis as taxi, against the terms and condition of policy, the Insurance
Company is not liable to pay compensation.
22. The Adv. for opponent placed Reliance upon another judgment
and Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Oriental Insurance Company Vs.
Parvesh Chander Chadha
in C.A.No. 6739 of 2010 decided on
17.8.2010 (S.C) wherein the Hon'ble Lordship of Apex Court observed
that-
"6. Admittedly, the Respondent had not informed the Appellant about
the alleged theft of the insured vehicle till he sent letter dated
22.5.1995 to the Branch Manager. In the complaint filed by him, the
Respondent did not give any explanation for this unusual delay in
informing the Appellant about the incident which gave rise to cause
for claiming compensation. Before the District Forum, the Respondent
did state that he had given copy of the first information report to
 13 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

Rajender Singh Pawar through whom he had insured the car and
untraced report prepared by police on 19.9.1995 was given to the
said Shri Rajender Singh Pawar, but his explanation was worthless
because in terms of the policy, the Respondent was required to inform
the Appellant about the theft of the insured vehicle. It is difficult, if
not impossible, to fathom any reason why the Respondent, who is
said to have lodged First Information Report on 20.1.1995 about the
theft of car did not inform the insurance company about the incident.
In terms of the policy issued by the Appellant, the Respondent was
duty bound to inform it about the theft of the vehicle immediately
after the incident. On account of delayed intimation, the Appellant
was deprived of its legitimate right to get an inquiry conducted into
the alleged theft of vehicle and make an endeavour to recover the
same. Unfortunately, all the consumer foras omitted to consider this
grave lapse on the part of the Respondent and directed the Appellant
to settle his claim on non-standard basis. In our view, the Appellant
cannot be saddled with the liability to pay compensation to the
Respondent despite the fact that he had not complied with the terms
of the policy."
23. The third reported case relied upon by the opponent Insurance
Company is
Puneet Kumar Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd
,. &
Anr. of National Commission in Revision Petition No. 308/2016 - of
Hon'ble National Commission wherein it is observed that, plying a
transport vehicle on a public place without the requisite permit
cannot be said merely to be breach of the warranty/condition of the
policy including limitation as to its use. Plying the vehicle on a public
place being prohibited and being punishable as an offence under the
 14 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

provision of the M.V.Act, such a breach in our view would be of a
fundamental nature and therefore will not fall within the purview of
the breach which in terms of the above referred guidelines can be
settled on non-standard basis.
In
Amalendu Sahoo
(Supra), the
private vehicle was found to be used for hire and such a breach was
not considered to be a fundamental breach of the terms and
conditions of the policy. The vehicle if registered for private use can
be brought on the road though it cannot be used for hire, whereas a
transport vehicle cannot at all be brought on the road without
obtaining the requisite permit in terms of the
section 66
of the
M.V.Act.
Therefore, the breach committed in this case cannot be
treated at par with the breach in
Amalendu Sahoo
(Supra).
24 We agree with the ratio of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble
National Commission in respect of use of vehicle by committing the
breach of condition as to limitation, wherein the claim may be
considered on non standard basis.
25. In the case in hand, it is important to note that, policy is
admittedly private car policy wherein it is one of the condition that,
the policy covers use of vehicle for any purpose other than hire or
reward or carrage of goods and in the schedule of policy it is made
clear that in case of use of private vehicle for hire and reward the
company shall not be liable to pay compensation. Here the vehicle is
used for hire and reward. In the statement of the injured Maya
Yogesh Bhalerao it is specifically mentioned that the driver was
collecting the passenger on hire and reward basis. She herself along
with her son Sanvidhan were travelling by paying fair with another
 15 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

passenger was Vinod Pardeshi who was injured and she learned that
he was expired. Said statement of witness is at page No. 73 of
appeal compilation. Copy of FIR is at page No. 29to30 which is
lodged by ASI Suresh Premchandu Jeere on next day on 10.5.2015 at
about 7.00 p.m. as the driver of vehicle ran away without giving
intimation to police station. In the said FIR also the name of
deceased Vinod Pardeshi and injured Maya Yogesh Bhalerao and her
son Sanvidhan is mentioned, who were travelling in the vehicle.
There is not a single statement given by complainant or his driver to
police that the friend of complainant were occupants. On the
contrary , the complainant for the first time is coming with the case
that the deceased was his friend and Maya Yogesh Bhalerao is the
wife and Sanvidhan is a son of his friend. These conducts of owner
and driver clearly shows that persons travelling were simply
passengers as submitted by passenger Maya Bhalerao, in her
statement before the police.
26. There is not a single document showing that the owner or
driver either came forward to give intimation to police or to
Insurance Company. Even before repudiating the claim the
opportunity was given to owner to submit explanation as to breach
of condition, i.e. carrying vehicle beyond limitation or breach of
policy condition and in causing delay of 48 days in submitting
intimation to Insurance company. When the opponent has
repudiated the claim on aforesaid grounds, then at least at the time
of filing the consumer complaint the complainant had opportunity to
explain these two conditions. The complainant remained silent to
state that as to why there is such a huge delay. On the bare
 16 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

statement of complaint that he gave intimation to police and the
intimation to service centre, it cannot be inferred that there was
intimation to Insurance Company. There is also no such document
showing that immediate instruction was given to police by the
complainant. Thus, there is no explanation for causing 48 days delay
in giving intimation to opponent Insurance Company. The
complainant has also not filed affidavit of insured Maya or her son
Sanvidhan if all they were wife and son of his friend.
27. If we go through the policy condition which is at page No.67,
states that, policy and its schedule, shall read together. The condition
No.1 at page No.67 as to condition, states that,-
"Notice shall be given in writing to the company immediately
upon the occurrence of any accidental loss or damage in the event of
any claim and thereafter the insured shall give all such information
and assistance as the company shall require."
28. It reveals from repudiation letter dated 29.05.20217 that,
besides the submission of claim there was no prior intimation of
incident to opponent Insurance Company. The repair estimation
issued by Diwekar garage to opponent in the month of January 2016,
(at page No.36to41) bears the claim number issued by opponent.
The said number is also mentioned in surveyor's report at page No.76
to 81 which show that, there was no prior intimation. The
complainant has also filed same documents, with his appeal
compilation of FA. No.290/2019, at page No. 28 to 80. Thus, even
on giving reasonable opportunity to explain the breach of policy
 17 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

conditions, the complainant failed to explain the same. There is also
no whisper that at any point of time the complainant made any
correspondence besides submission of claim to opponent.
On the
contrary the complainant or his driver did not visit police station
after accident or issued intimation to opponent Insurance company
as required immediately after the incident, as to loss or damage
sustained to vehicle, in writing. This delay of 48 days is inordinate
and not at all explained satisfactorily as expected as per conditions
and also observed by the judgment of Apex Court in Oriental
Insurance Com. Ltd,. Vs. Parvesh Chandar Chadda, Stated Supra and
even as observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Omprakash Vs.
Reliance General Insurance, Stated Supra
. It is expected to explain
the delay satisfactorily. In the case in hand it is not at all explained.
29. Secondly, the another breach as to driving the vehicle for hire
or reward beyond the condition as to use of vehicle beyond
limitation is not only breach but using the vehicle without permit in
contravention of the provision of
Motor Vehicle Act
. Perhaps even if
it is accepted in view of
Amlendu
's case that the claim for breach of
such condition can be settled on non standard basis, still in the case
in hand there is breach of condition as to intimation of accident
immediately to the Insurance Company in writing, and it is inordinate
delay of 48 days it is not explained as mentioned above.
30. The Hon'ble District Consumer Forum though observed that
there is breach of policy condition and further pleased to allow the
complaint partly on non standard basis, by ignoring fact that the case
is relied upon by the opponent states that delay in lodging report if
 18 FA/206 & 290 of 2019

not explained properly or satisfactorily the Insurance Company
cannot be held liable to pay compensation to the insured. At the cost
of repetition we would like to mention that, in this case the District
Consumer Forum has totally ignored that in spite of giving
opportunity by opponent Insurance Company to the complainant to
explain the delay & breach of policy condition, there is no
explanation and also no whisper about the same. Therefore, in
aforesaid distinguishing circumstances, it cannot be said that the
claim is repudiated only on technical ground.
31. Moreover, immediate conduct on the part of driver, fleeing
away from the spot without intimation of accident and further on the
part of owner not giving information immediately in writing to the
insurance company as expected in policy condition, not make
entitled the complainant the compensation. Hence, the judgment
of District Consumer Forum requires interference and needs to be set
aside. There is also no merits in appeal filed by complainant for
enhanced compensation as claimed in the complaint. We therefore,
answer the points accordingly and pass following order.
ORDER
1. The appeal No.206/2019 filed by Bajaj
 Allianz General Insurance Company is
 hereby allowed and the judgment & order in
 C.C.No.72/2018 is hereby set aside.
Consequently complaint No.72/2018 is
 hereby dismissed.
19 FA/206 & 290 of 2019
2. The appeal No. 290/2019 filed by Deepak
 Manikrao Lolge is hereby dismissed.
3. No order as to costs.
4. Certified copy of this judgment be placed
 in A/290/2019.
Mr.K.M.Lawande Smt.S.T.Barne,
 Member Presiding Judicial Member

UNK
